chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Salih ibn Razin and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Every eye will be weeping on the Day of Judgment except three eyes: an eye that lowered its gaze from the prohibitions of Allah, or an eye that stayed awake in the worship of Allah, or an eye that wept in the middle of the night out of the fear of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of eyes that will not weep on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) categorizes the 'eyes' as instruments of spiritual accountability, distinguishing between passive restraint from sin, active vigilance in worship, and the profound emotional state of *khashyah* (awe). The inclusion of weeping in the 'depths of the night' underscores the Shia emphasis on *Qiyam al-Layl* and the transformative power of nocturnal devotion in purifying the soul before the final reckoning.
